Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Church life · Time, the calendar & feasts

Good Friday noun

also Great Friday, Holy Friday

late Latin

Vulg. Jo. 19.31
Vulg. Mc. 15.42
Tert. Adv. Marc. 4.12 (Lewis & Short)

Parascēvē, Parascēvēs f.

noun

Good Friday, the day of Preparation

Greek παρασκευή, the day of preparation before the Sabbath, the Friday of the Passion (Lewis & Short). In Greek every Friday is still παρασκευή, and this one is Great Friday (Μεγάλη Παρασκευή).

Other words

  • Fēria Sexta in Parascēvē — Good Friday

    also used · medieval · Miss. Rōm., Fer. VI in Parascēvē (Latinitas Precēs)

    The Roman Missal’s name for the day.

Examples

  • quia erat parascēvē, quod est ante sabbatum

    because it was the day of Preparation, the day before the SabbathVulg. Mc. 15.42

See also Holy Week, Easter, Palm Sunday.

SourcesLewis & Short: parasceve · Lewis & Short: feriae
